## New to this theme? {#why-this-theme-matters}

A new model can fail because it cannot run, because it violates an input or
output contract, because it lacks needed evidence, or because it makes a poor
answer despite having that evidence. These are different failures, so a model
family should not receive a permanent verdict from one small panel.

For example, a model that accepts frames and audio has passed a compatibility
check, not an answer-quality check. If a later answer is wrong because the
needed moment was never supplied, replacing or fine-tuning the answerer targets
the wrong bottleneck.

<span id="technical-summary" class="legacy-fragment-alias" aria-hidden="true"></span>

## Current working answer

Use the frozen-30 protocol-v2 comparison for current model selection. Keep
Qwen3.5-4B with 12 frames as the **Current default** for accuracy and MiniCPM-o
4.5 audio-off as the **Fast alternate**. Treat newer/larger candidates as
**Diagnostic signal**, **Routed candidate**, or **Open hypothesis** until they
complete a matched, label-isolated quality comparison. Qwen3-Omni A4 completed
that comparison but did not meet the general-model or native-audio promotion
gate. VideoChat3-4B completed a focused comparison but did not earn a
Temporal/Action specialist role.

::: {.theme-decision-strip aria-label="Model decisions"}
- **Use now:** Qwen3.5-4B with 12 frames; use MiniCPM-o audio-off for speed.
- **Do not default:** the pinned VideoChat3-4B checkpoint under either tested
  fixed-12- or fixed-24-frame condition, or later candidates based on
  compatibility or selected screens alone.
- **Still possible:** repaired Omni, narrower Omni audio routing, specialist
  models, and bottleneck-first adaptation.
- **Next test:** use the existing A4 six-change screen as a provisional
  mechanism hypothesis, not a completed audit: five target changes are
  consistent with acoustic sensitivity, while one control `C→W` regression is
  consistent with cross-modal interference or downstream answer selection.
  First measure required-evidence recall, oracle-evidence answering, and
  end-to-end answering before any routed run or adaptation.
:::

## Evidence at a glance

- **Strongest comparison:** frozen-30 protocol v2 supports the current Qwen and
  MiniCPM roles on labeled 2025 training data.
- **Selected diagnostics:** Qwen3.6, Phi, Gemma, and Omni screens do not rank
  their families globally.
- **Multiple-choice diagnostic:** the selected 20-row MC screen places Gemini
  native AV ahead of both Qwen3.6 views and blind fusion, but is not a
  representative promotion benchmark; see the
  [routing-owned claim](research-routing.{{< meta report-ext >}}#mc-poc20).
- **Completed Omni result:** A4 produced `60/60` eligible outputs; frames-only
  failed the 4B general-model gate, while audio-on showed target gains but one
  control `C→W` regression.
- **Historical attempts:** A1/A2 failed at the dstack runner boundary and A3
  exposed bulk-file transport as the bottleneck; the private bundle path
  resolved execution without changing the scientific condition.
- **Verified negative:** at both 12 and 24 fixed frames, VideoChat3-4B improved
  only `1/4` selected Temporal/Action targets and regressed both Visual
  controls against the matched Qwen3.5-4B baseline.
- **Historical confirmed defect:** one Qwen3-Omni strict output missed the
  earlier 20/20 completion gate; A4 later completed `60/60` without changing
  that historical result.
- **Condition boundary:** no small screen permanently disqualifies a model,
  checkpoint, evidence route, or later adaptation.

## What has been tried

### Full-panel Qwen3.5-4B baseline extension {#qwen35-full-panel-baseline}

- **Reason for testing:** extend the established 30-row visual baseline to
  every 2025 training row that has both an annotation and local media, and
  measure whether a remote GPU makes that larger evidence boundary practical.
- **Tested condition and panel:** Qwen3.5-4B with the pinned revision and 12
  uniform temporal midpoint frames on 475 locally available VQA 2025 training
  rows. Six of the 481 annotation records had no local video and were excluded
  before inference. VQA testing, VQA 2026, and VTT caption/search rows were not
  part of this quality panel.
- **Observed result:** all `475/475` label-free inference rows completed. The
  local diagnostic score was `0.090526` normalized exact match, `0.240696`
  token F1, and `0.156063` lexical METEOR. The known 30-row overlap reproduced
  the prior baseline exactly (`0.300000` exact match and `0.430725` token F1).
  On an NVIDIA L40S, frame preparation took `1,932.15` seconds and model
  workload took `531.50` seconds; the dstack task cost approximately `$0.72`.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Verified full-panel baseline
  reference; not a promotion comparison.** Retain Qwen3.5-4B with 12 frames
  as the visual control for the next matched evidence experiment.
- **What this rules out now:** treating the 475-row Qwen baseline as
  unmeasured, or assuming that local execution requires the earlier roughly
  twelve-hour estimate when a comparable L40S is available.
- **What it does not rule out:** a different model, grounding gains,
  answer-selection failures, or performance on the unlabeled 2025 test and
  2026 collections. The related [matched full-panel Whisper/frame
  audit](research-speech-transcripts.{{< meta report-ext >}}#matched-full-panel-frame-audio-audit)
  is recorded under Speech and Transcript Evidence rather than duplicated
  here; the single visual condition itself cannot establish a winning
  solution.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—the full
  annotation JSONs do not carry the category taxonomy used by selected
  development panels, so this record reports aggregate metrics rather than a
  post-hoc category leaderboard. The metrics are local diagnostics, not an
  official competition submission score.
- **Reconsider when:** a label-blind matched Whisper/grounding arm freezes on
  the same 475 IDs and produces a paired improvement with predeclared
  non-regression rules; do not rerun this control unless the inference contract
  changes.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The input manifest contained only `video_id` and `question`; annotation answers
and incorrect answers were loaded only after the remote predictions froze. The
run used the pinned CUDA image and Transformers revision recorded in the
[sanitized score artifact](../../docs/experiments/artifacts/qwen35-4b-12f-full-20260803-c1-score.json).
Remote prediction and output checksum manifests were verified locally. The
[canonical run plan](../../plans/qwen35-475-dstack.md) preserves the input
boundary, immutable run identifiers, and the next decision. The score uses the
repository's normalized exact-match and token-F1 diagnostic contract; METEOR
was computed locally with the deterministic lexical-only convention. Raw
media, predictions, annotations, credentials, and private bucket locators are
not included in this hub.
</details>

### Three-video compatibility gate {#compatibility-gate-models}

- **Reason for testing:** determine which adapters can execute under a shared
  label-blind input contract before spending on a larger quality panel.
- **Tested condition and panel:** five model families on three deliberately
  different labeled 2025 examples.
- **Observed result:** Qwen, Molmo, InternVL, and Gemma completed all requested
  inferences; MiniCPM completed two of three and had a speech-row input error.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Diagnostic signal** for portability and
  adapter behavior, not a model leaderboard.
- **What this rules out now:** promoting a family or estimating its competition
  quality from three execution rows.
- **What it does not rule out:** a repaired adapter or a matched larger quality
  panel for any compatible family.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—three selected
  rows are a portability screen, not a quality ranking.
- **Reconsider when:** the candidate completes a declared, label-isolated
  quality panel with the same evidence and scoring controls as its comparator.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The compatibility gate checks that a combined request can execute; it does not
score semantic answer quality. The [three-video gate report · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/three_video_gate_results_2026-07-20.md)
and [Experiment Integrity and Evaluation](research-integrity.{{< meta report-ext >}}#compatibility-gate)
describe why that distinction matters.
</details>

### Failure-selected Qwen3.6 screen {#failure-panel}

- **Reason for testing:** learn whether a larger Qwen model recovers known
  visual, audio, and temporal failures that the baseline missed.
- **Tested condition and panel:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B used the same 12 frames as
  the baseline across 12 deliberately selected failures.
- **Observed result:** it was `3C/2P/7W`, compared with `4C/4P/4W` for the
  strongest tested visual and audio-off alternatives. It recovered three
  baseline failures but had a visual-control regression and confident wrong
  music/instrument answers.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition** as a replacement for the current baseline.
- **What this rules out now:** advancing this Qwen3.6 version, prompt, and
  12-frame configuration from the 12-row failure panel.
- **What it does not rule out:** a different Qwen3.6 revision, evidence
  policy, question route, or representative matched panel.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—the 12 rows
  were selected failures and include a visual-control regression.
- **Reconsider when:** a compatibility-cleared version passes a predeclared
  matched specialist or representative quality gate without control loss.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The run itself was technically clean, so this is not a runtime failure. The
failure-selected panel can reveal recovery patterns but cannot estimate full
test accuracy; the 24-frame local winner on this panel is superseded as a
global default by frozen-30. See the [failure-panel report · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/failure_panel_qwen36_audio_results_2026-07-24.md).
</details>

### VideoChat3 Temporal/Action specialist screen {#videochat3-temporal-specialist}

- **Canonical model-eligibility claim:** this record owns the project decision
  for the pinned VideoChat3-4B fixed-12- and fixed-24-frame conditions.
- **Reason for testing:** upstream presents VideoChat3-4B as an efficient,
  fully open generalist video model with an I3D video encoder, adaptive frame
  resolution, and general, long-form, and streaming-video training. The project
  tested the narrower hypothesis that those video-centric capabilities would
  recover known Temporal/Action failures better than Qwen3.5-4B. This was a
  project hypothesis, not an upstream guarantee of superiority on this VQA
  slice.
- **Tested condition and panel:** four predeclared Temporal/Action targets and
  two Visual controls first used identical cached 12-frame evidence for both
  pinned models. A three-advisor review then unanimously selected one terminal
  matched 24-frame offline screen because it doubled VideoChat3's I3D temporal
  chunks from three to six while preserving the competition input contract.
  Both conditions held original frame indices and timestamps, prompt, seed,
  greedy decoding, and 32-token cap fixed.
- **Observed result:** at 12 frames, both models completed `6/6`; VideoChat3
  scored `0C/2P/4W` against Qwen's `2C/2P/2W`, improved `1/4` targets, tied
  `2/4`, regressed `1/4`, and regressed both controls. At 24 frames, the
  exact-image canary passed `1/1`, both models passed the matched gate `2/2`,
  and both completed `6/6`; VideoChat3 scored `0C/1P/5W` against Qwen's
  `3C/2P/1W`, improved `1/4` targets, regressed `3/4`, and again regressed both
  controls. Qwen-24 improved `1/6` versus Qwen-12 with no regressions, so a
  weakened 24-frame comparator does not explain the loss. Both tests missed
  the predeclared at-least-`2/4` target gains and zero-control-regression rule.
- **Evidence validity:** **Verified**. Predictions were frozen before references
  or grades were loaded. The 12-frame graders agreed on `11/12` candidate
  grades before one adjudication; the 24-frame graders agreed on all `12/12`
  grades, requiring no adjudication. The 24-frame runner verified the complete
  manifest hash, cache records, timestamps, and all 144 frame hashes before
  model loading. A post-run integration audit independently re-read all three
  executed frozen pilot manifests (`3ab0fc1…`, `8b5cf944…`, and `d13a1135…`),
  verified their full SHA-256 values, and found only the explicit inference
  allowlist (`run_id`, `condition_id`, `video_id`, `question`, frame evidence,
  transcript, plus the 24-frame cache key). No answer, annotation, reference,
  label, grade, gold, ground-truth, or score field was present. The reusable
  selector now rejects unexpected fields before projecting the allowlist.
- **Decision disposition:** **Not promoted under the tested condition**.
- **What this rules out now:** using the pinned VideoChat3 revision and this
  tested fixed-12- and fixed-24-frame input flows as a Temporal/Action
  specialist over the pinned Qwen baseline on the frozen panel. No additional
  frame-count, prompt, raw-video, adaptive, or streaming test of this checkpoint
  is justified for the current offline competition pipeline.
- **What it does not rule out:** the model family on other rows, a materially
  different future checkpoint, task-specific fine-tuning, or performance on a
  representative benchmark. Adaptive and streaming modes remain untested, but
  the advisor review rejected them as the next competition test because they
  change the matched offline task rather than isolate the density hypothesis.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—the six rows
  were purposively selected rather than representative. No surviving
  input-flow defect was found. **Audit gap**—a credential-bearing local startup
  trace was deleted during containment, so its full environment line cannot be
  reconstructed; the submitted snapshot and checksum-verifiable inference and
  grading evidence remain available, so this does not invalidate the quality
  comparison. Private bucket coordinates, relative object names, and row-level
  grades remain outside the research hub; only aggregate evidence classes,
  aggregate grades, and checksum evidence are tracked.
- **Reconsider when:** a materially different checkpoint, task-specific
  adaptation, or representative benchmark creates a new hypothesis—not another
  input variation of this technically complete checkpoint because its quality
  was poor.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The tested revisions were `MCG-NJU/VideoChat3-4B@37fa901ec5913f84bc31108ebc1e60ad1903634c`
and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B@851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`.
CUDA BF16 inference ran on an NVIDIA A40 using the pinned
`docker.io/pytorch/pytorch@sha256:b85566342b86d13a67712e9315d40cdc2dad7f8d86df1aff3831f80835edbcca`
image. The completed 12-frame dev session cost `$0.1420`; cumulative VideoChat3
work was `$0.6572`. The terminal 24-frame dev session cost `$0.0763`, bringing
cumulative VideoChat3 work to `$0.7335`. Private input, prediction, and grading
bundles were listed, downloaded, and checksum-verified; raw rows, answers,
media, logs, and private artifact locators are intentionally excluded from this
hub. See the
[sanitized terminal retired record · Evidence of record · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/b8f80f00fa97fbdaddd08a143b4809a38809e456/dstack/videochat3-24frame-dev-20260801-a1.retired.yml),
[official model card · Upstream model description](https://huggingface.co/MCG-NJU/VideoChat3-4B),
and [official paper page · Upstream research claim](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.14935).
</details>

### Phi and Gemma semantic screen {#phi-gemma-semantic-stop}

- **Reason for testing:** separate successful joint audio/vision compatibility
  from meaningful answer quality for two non-Qwen candidates.
- **Tested condition and panel:** after a three-role joint-modality
  compatibility probe, Phi-4-multimodal-instruct and Gemma 3n ran a corrected
  semantic screen over three selected audio roles.
- **Observed result:** Gemma was `1C/1P/1W`; Phi was `0C/2P/1W`. An earlier
  compatibility-only Gemma promotion is superseded by this quality screen.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition** beyond the three-row semantic screen.
- **What this rules out now:** using successful combined-modality parsing, or
  the earlier compatibility promotion, as evidence that either tested version
  improves answer quality.
- **What it does not rule out:** a newer checkpoint, a repaired input path, a
  different evidence route, or a larger representative comparison.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—the three-row
  semantic screen is too small to rank either family.
- **Reconsider when:** a candidate first passes compatibility and then meets a
  predeclared semantic-quality and control non-regression gate on a matched
  panel.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The counts are a semantic screen, not a general leaderboard. The relevant
records are the [compatibility probe · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/docs/experiments/2026-07-24-nonqwen-omni-compatibility.md)
and [semantic-quality correction · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/docs/experiments/2026-07-24-omni-semantic-quality.md).
</details>

### MiniCPM-o 4.5 fast alternate {#minicpm-fast-alternate}

- **Reason for testing:** compare a practical native-video model with the
  visual Qwen conditions under frozen-30's shared protocol.
- **Tested condition and panel:** MiniCPM-o 4.5 with native-video input and
  audio disabled across all 30 frozen rows.
- **Observed result:** it achieved the best METEOR (`0.374089`) and fastest
  measured outer wall time (4.50 minutes), while Qwen plus quality-gated
  Whisper led exact match and token F1.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Fast alternate**, not the global
  accuracy winner on every metric.
- **What this rules out now:** calling MiniCPM-o the global accuracy winner
  under frozen-30 merely because it was fastest or led METEOR.
- **What it does not rule out:** using it when latency dominates, quality on
  other representative panels, or a future accuracy/latency frontier under a
  different controlled environment.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—the outer-wall
  timing is environment-specific and frozen-30 is descriptive 2025 training
  evidence.
- **Reconsider when:** a repeated same-hardware matched panel jointly reports
  completion, latency, exact/F1, and the declared speed-quality decision rule.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

All four frozen-30 conditions completed 30/30 rows. This is descriptive model
selection on labeled 2025 training data, not an estimate for the unlabeled
2026 evaluation set. See the [protocol-v2 report · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md).
</details>

### Qwen3-Omni quality and completion gate {#qwen3-omni-quality}

- **Canonical model-eligibility claim:** its stable identity is
  `#qwen3-omni-quality`; the related
  [Canonical native-audio-effect claim](research-native-audio.{{< meta report-ext >}}#qwen3-omni-native-audio)
  is owned by Native Audio.
- **Reason for testing:** test a joint native-audio candidate under a paired
  frames-only/audio-on contract after its runtime became compatible.
- **Tested condition and panel:** 10 deliberately difficult rows, 12 sampled
  frames with and without native audio, a modality-neutral prompt, and a
  predeclared 20/20 strict-output completion requirement.
- **Observed result:** the diagnostic semantic comparison was `3C/3P/4W`
  frames-only and `5C/2P/3W` audio-on, but the unchanged strict run completed
  19/20 outputs because one complete answer used fenced JSON.
- **Current condition-bound status:** formally ineligible under the
  predeclared 20/20 completion gate; **Not promoted under the tested
  condition**, while remaining a **Routed candidate** for a repaired run.
- **What this rules out now:** using the incomplete strict run for a promotion
  decision or declaring Qwen3-Omni the new general baseline.
- **What it does not rule out:** the model family, a repaired parser/output
  contract, a complete blinded paired run, or specialist native-audio value.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Confirmed defect**—one
  fenced output failed the unchanged strict parser and completion gate.
- **Reconsider when:** a sentinel verifies the output fix and a fresh full
  20-call paired run completes under one frozen configuration and its declared
  quality/control gate.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The earlier A1 run completed 20/20 strict outputs but had a prompt-context
mismatch and did not meet its semantic gate. The neutral A2 rerun corrected
that prompt context but one strict-parser failure remained. Semantic recovery
of that exact output is diagnostic only and cannot retroactively complete A2.
The 10 rows are selected and frame-based, so they cannot be compared directly
to frozen-30. 2026 answer quality remains unknown.
See the [quality-10 report · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/docs/experiments/2026-07-25-qwen3-omni-quality-10.md)
and [neutral A2 result · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub](https://github.com/npatta01/trec_video_2026/blob/814e55429f6dd1dc8570bc08f1dad849f74e36a1/docs/experiments/2026-07-25-qwen3-omni-quality-10-neutral-a2.md).
</details>

### Qwen3-Omni frozen-30 execution and model result {#qwen3-omni-frozen30-runner-attempts}

- **Canonical related claim:** Models owns the general-model disposition. The
  [Native Audio claim](research-native-audio.{{< meta report-ext >}}#qwen3-omni-native-audio)
  owns the primary modality decision from the same A4 evidence.
- **Shared evidence bundle and immutable evidence link:** [A4 evidence of
  record](../../docs/experiments/2026-07-31-qwen3-omni-frozen30.md),
  [sanitized A4 score](../../docs/experiments/artifacts/qwen3-omni-frozen30-a4-score.json),
  and [historical infrastructure record](../../docs/experiments/2026-07-30-qwen3-omni-frozen30-infrastructure-attempts.md).
- **Evidence validity:** **Verified** for the exact paired A4 model conditions;
  historical A1/A2/A3 failures remain infrastructure evidence only.
- **Decision disposition:** **Not promoted under the tested condition** as a
  general-model candidate. Keep Qwen3.5-4B with twelve frames as the accuracy
  baseline.
- **Decision rule and predeclaration:** frames-only had to meet baseline exact
  match `0.300000` and token F1 `0.430725`, with no six-row stratum losing more
  than one exact answer.
- **Gate outcome and completion denominator:** A4 completed `60/60` strict
  outputs. Frames-only scored exact `0.233333` and F1 `0.418762`; its
  spatial/OCR/color stratum was `4/6` exact versus the baseline's `6/6`. All
  three general-model clauses failed.
- **Supersedes / superseded by:** A4 supersedes the pending quality unknown and
  completed-run retry requirement. It does not erase A1/A2/A3 or the earlier
  quality-10 diagnostics.
- **Reason for testing:** obtain a complete matched result for the pinned Omni
  checkpoint and decide whether it merits either a general or routed role.
- **Tested condition and panel:** the balanced labeled-2025 frozen-30 panel,
  the same twelve frames in both conditions, native WAV only in audio-on,
  neutral prompt, deterministic decoding, and labels only after prediction
  freeze.
- **Observed result:** frames-only did not displace the 4B baseline. Audio-on
  improved overall exact/F1/METEOR to `0.267 / 0.445 / 0.345`, but failed its
  separate route-safety gate because one control changed `C→W`.
- **Current condition-bound status:** complete, eligible, and **Not promoted
  under the tested condition** for either declared role.
- **What this rules out now:** selecting the 30B Omni checkpoint as the general
  visual default, or treating its larger size and successful execution as
  evidence of better answer quality.
- **What it does not rule out:** a narrower dialogue/prosody specialist,
  another evidence policy, or a later checkpoint tested under the same gate.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—A4 does not
  isolate whether its five target changes came from evidence access,
  representation, fusion, or answer selection, or whether the control
  regression reflects cross-modal competition, representation, or downstream
  answer selection. The post-hoc screen is a mechanism hypothesis, not causal
  proof. Two scorer-schema omissions were repaired through exact allowlists,
  preserved freezes, and byte-identical score reproduction.
- **Reconsider when:** a label-blind failure audit produces a pre-answer route
  feature that explains the target wins without the control regression, or a
  different checkpoint passes the unchanged general-model gate.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

A1 and A2 failed before inference at the dstack runner boundary. D1 and the C1
task canary later proved runner/task startup. A3 then showed the remaining
bottleneck: 445 dstack mappings transported about 318 MB serially and could not
finish before runner startup. A4 replaced only that transport with one private,
immutable Hugging Face bundle. Its exact non-development bundle canary passed,
and the H200 dev workload completed and synced all artifacts. A4 cost `$3.2901`
including its bundle canary; historical identities, costs, and limitations are
retained in the infrastructure report.
</details>

### Seeded termination-repair follow-up {#qwen3-omni-seeded-termination-repair}

- **Reason for testing:** determine whether the prior non-EOS failure could be
  reproduced and contained before another paid quality comparison.
- **Tested condition and panel:** the same thirty frames-only frozen examples,
  visual-concise instruction, pinned model/runtime/evidence, and explicit
  sampled decoding (`temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`), with a new
  sealed seed `42` rather than the earlier `20260724` seed.
- **Observed result:** the development run completed `30/30` rows in expected
  order. Every row parsed, used seed `42`, and ended with EOS; the prior
  `Hw0bRvn1ZIo` row (`pair_index=18`) ended at `845` tokens.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Verified execution repair for the
  sealed seed-42 profile; no promotion weight.** This is completion evidence,
  not a new semantic comparison.
- **What this rules out now:** treating the earlier cap-without-EOS event as
  an unresolved blocker for this sealed execution profile.
- **What it does not rule out:** recurrence under another seed or workload,
  and it does not change the A4 quality decision or baseline selection.
- **Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty:** **Uncertainty**—this is one
  explicitly selected seed; the termination gate now records seed, final token,
  and EOS status and fails closed on a future cap-without-EOS row.
- **Reconsider when:** a future matched specialist-quality question is
  predeclared, or a different sealed seed reproduces the failure often enough
  to justify a bounded reliability probe.

## Known failures and cases

[CASE-004 — Unsupported native-audio specificity](failure-library.{{< meta report-ext >}}#case-004)
illustrates why a more capable modality path can still produce a worse,
over-specific answer. Diagnose evidence, fusion, and output-contract failures
before treating the model family as the cause.

### What the evidence supports

- A successful adapter or joint-modality request proves compatibility, not
  semantic answer quality.
- MiniCPM-o audio-off is a useful speed/METEOR trade-off, while Qwen3.5-4B
  remains the current accuracy baseline.
- The tested Qwen3.6, Phi, and Gemma conditions did not earn promotion; their
  results bound those versions, evidence paths, and small panels.
- Qwen3-Omni A4 is complete quality evidence: frames-only failed the general
  gate, while native audio showed target gains but failed control safety.
- Bundle transport, model execution, output completion, and answer quality are
  separate boundaries; A4 resolved the first three and measured the fourth.
- The pinned VideoChat3-4B checkpoint did not earn a Temporal/Action specialist
  role because both fixed-12- and fixed-24-frame comparisons missed the
  target-improvement threshold and regressed both controls.
- Qwen3-Omni's earlier quality-10 run had no eligible promotion result because
  its strict completion gate was not met; A4 is the complete matched result.

### What it does not rule out

- No small screen permanently disqualifies a model family, model revision, or
  specialist route.
- Frozen-30 does not prove the baseline is best on unlabeled 2026 evaluation.
- Compatibility, completion, semantic quality, and cost are separate gates;
  passing one cannot substitute for the others.
- Fine-tuning may be useful later, but no current result identifies a measured
  bottleneck that warrants it over evidence selection or answer grounding.

<span id="possible-bugs-confounds-and-audit-gaps" class="legacy-fragment-alias" aria-hidden="true"></span>

### Confirmed defects, audit gaps, and uncertainties

- **Historical confirmed defect:** the quality-10 Omni run missed one strict
  output; A4 later passed `60/60` without changing that historical result.
- **Uncertainty:** Qwen3.6, Phi, and Gemma panels are selected diagnostics; A4
  is balanced frozen-30 evidence but still not a 2026 estimate.
- **Uncertainty:** Qwen3.6, Phi, Gemma, Omni, and VideoChat3 quality panels are
  selected diagnostics, not representative rankings or 2026 estimates.
- **Audit gap:** the VideoChat3 24-frame local startup trace was deleted during
  credential containment, so its full environment line cannot be reconstructed;
  preserved checksummed inference and grading evidence is not affected.
- **Uncertainty:** model comparison can be confounded by frame policy, prompt,
  modality treatment, and answer formatting unless they are held fixed.
- **Audit gap:** the repository has compatibility and experimental seams, not
  one reusable versioned model-promotion workflow for every candidate family.
- **Resolved execution bottleneck:** A3 instrumentation showed that serial
  transport of 445 mapped files could not finish before runner startup; A4's
  immutable bundle path passed its canary and completed the workload.

## Open hypotheses and ideas

- A narrow Qwen3-Omni audio-relevant route may retain A4's five target wins
  while excluding its one control regression.
- Native audio may increase acoustic sensitivity on audio-relevant rows while
  competing with other available evidence on control rows; this remains a
  **Cross-modal competition hypothesis** until required-evidence and
  oracle-answer measurements exist.
- A grounded answer-election or evidence-citation guard may preserve visible
  text and spatial answers when audio is present, but it should be tested only
  after evidence availability is measured.
- A specialist model may beat the baseline on a declared evidence type even if
  it is not a global replacement.
- Adaptation or fine-tuning should follow a measured bottleneck diagnosis.
  Model fine-tuning is justified for fusion or answer-selection failures only
  after retrieval and the supplied evidence have been controlled; a measured
  retrieval failure instead calls for evidence-selection work first.

## Cheapest valid next experiments

### Qwen3-Omni error-mechanism audit {#repaired-complete-neutral-qwen3-omni-run}

- **Hypothesis:** A4's five audio target wins and single control regression can
  be separated by a pre-answer evidence or route feature rather than by model
  size or post-hoc answer quality.
- **Current hypothesis from existing evidence:** the frozen six
  decision-relevant changes contain five target improvements in the declared
  dialogue/speech and sound/music target strata, consistent with gains from
  acoustic evidence. The one
  control `C→W` regression is consistent with cross-modal competition, audio
  distraction, or downstream answer selection. This is not a completed
  label-blind audit or a causal result; A4 does not establish the mechanism.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Diagnostic signal** with an unresolved
  **Audit gap**; no new model run is justified by this screen alone.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** create a private, label-blind audit
  sheet for the six changes that freezes each row's minimum required modality
  and evidence before revealing condition or grade. Record required-evidence
  presence/recall per condition, oracle-evidence answer quality, and original
  end-to-end answer quality. Keep the four other control `C↔P`/`W↔C` shifts in
  the safety analysis rather than treating them as target wins.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** preserve A4 bytes, hashes, and
  paired identities; annotate required evidence independently of model answers;
  hide condition and grade until the evidence labels are frozen; keep route
  design separate from the outcomes used to motivate it; keep private row data
  out of the durable report.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** pursue retrieval or routing work only when
  required-evidence recall is limiting and oracle evidence improves answers;
  pursue fusion/grounding or answer election when necessary evidence is
  present but the model remains wrong; test modality competition when audio-on
  reduces visual evidence sufficiency or visual-control quality. Any later
  route must retain the existing audio-off fallback and control-safety gate.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** a falsifiable next
  routing or grounding experiment for this labeled slice, not a general-model
  promotion, prevalence estimate, or deployed specialist.

### Representative matched specialist-model panel

- **Hypothesis:** a compatibility-cleared model can add value on a declared
  specialist stratum without harming matched controls.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a frozen representative slice with
  target and visual/temporal control strata, after a three-row compatibility
  check if the adapter changed.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** same frames, modality policy,
  prompt, decoding, scoring, labels-after-freeze boundary, and baseline model;
  record model revision and input/output contracts.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** promote only if the candidate meets a paired
  target-stratum gain and route-level non-regression threshold.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** a specialist role on
  that panel, not a general leaderboard position.

### Bottleneck-first adaptation decision

- **Hypothesis:** adaptation is justified only when a measured retrieval,
  fusion, or answer-selection bottleneck remains after evidence paths freeze.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a small grounded development slice
  that reports selector recall, oracle-evidence answer quality, and end-to-end
  answer quality before any training run.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** hold base model, evidence,
  prompts, labels-after-freeze boundary, and scoring fixed; compare any adapted
  model to the unadapted baseline on held-out rows.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** authorize adaptation only when the diagnostic
  identifies a residual bottleneck and held-out non-regression is predeclared.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** value for the
  declared adaptation and panel, not a blanket claim that fine-tuning solves
  video QA.
